title: Prefix Sums and Prefix Products
summary: Precompute running totals so any range sum becomes a subtraction instead of a scan.
keyPoints: A prefix array stores the total of everything before each index.
The sum of a range is prefix[right] - prefix[left], which is O(1) after O(n) preprocessing.
Prefix arrays use half-open ranges: [left, right) is prefix[right] - prefix[left].
A prefix sum plus a hash map counts subarrays with a target sum in one pass.
Prefix and suffix products can replace division when zeroes make division unsafe.

complexity.note: One extra entry for the empty prefix.
Prefix sum plus a frequency map.
Output can use O(1) extra if allowed.

commonMistakes: Using prefix[right] - prefix[left] when the range should include the right endpoint.
Forgetting the empty prefix in the frequency map, which misses subarrays that start at index 0.
Dividing by zero in a prefix-product problem when the input contains zeroes.
Building prefix sums but then scanning the range again anyway.
interviewNotes: Define the prefix array clearly: `prefix[i]` is the sum of the first i items, or the sum before index i. Mixing conventions causes off-by-one bugs.
If the problem asks for many range queries, mention that O(n) preprocessing buys O(1) queries.
For subarray counts, explain why the map stores frequencies rather than indices.

checkYourself.question: What is prefix[4] if prefix[0] is the empty sum?
checkYourself.answer: It is the sum of the first four items, at indices 0 through 3.

checkYourself.question: Why does the subarray-counting map start with {0: 1}?
checkYourself.answer: The empty prefix has sum 0. Counting it lets a subarray that starts at index 0 be found when the current prefix sum equals the target.

checkYourself.question: Why use prefix and suffix products instead of dividing the total product?
checkYourself.answer: Division fails when a value is zero, and may be inaccurate for some numeric types. A prefix and suffix pass avoids division entirely.
